transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, uh… thanks, Doctor. I guess what brings me in is… I’m worried about how I get with food at night. It’s like, I’ll just start picking at something, you know, maybe after everything’s quiet, and I tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then my hand just keeps going back.

It sounds silly when I say it out loud. I work in shipping and receiving, so I’m used to keeping track of things, counts, boxes, what goes where… but with this, it’s like I don’t get to make the decision anymore once I’ve started. That part scares me a little.
Can you tell me more about what happens when you start eating at night? Do you find yourself eating a lot more than you intended in a short amount of time?

Yeah… yeah, I do. Not every single night, but some nights after work, I’ll be in the kitchen and it starts like I’m just putting things away or cleaning up leftovers. And then I’ll have, like… several tamales, and then a big bowl of pozole if there’s some there, tortillas, whatever rice or beans are left.

I’m standing there the whole time, too, like I’m not even sitting down for dinner. It’s weird because at work I’m careful with inventory, like if a box is short I notice right away, but at home I’ll look and half the food’s gone before I really… admit that I ate it. So yes, it ends up being way more than I meant to in a pretty short time.
When you’re eating at night like that, does it feel like you can’t stop or control how much you’re eating, even if you want to?

Yeah… that’s the part that bothers me. Once I start, I’ll tell myself, like, okay, that’s enough, Santiago, put it away. And then I’m still there, opening the container again or reaching for one more thing.

It’s strange because I can control myself with other stuff, you know, like at work if I’m counting pallets or checking labels, I can stop and double-check everything. But with the food late at night, it feels like my hand just keeps going back before I’ve really decided anything. Like I’m not fully the one calling the shots in that moment.
When you're eating at night like this, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yeah… I mean, yes. By the time I finally stop, my stomach feels really tight and heavy. Like I overpacked a box, you know, and now the seams are kind of… not literally, but that’s how it feels.

Sometimes I end up just sitting on the edge of the couch for a while because if I bend over, or try to lie down, it feels bad. I’ll tell myself I should just go to bed, but then I’m sitting there waiting for that heavy feeling to calm down.
When you're eating at night like this, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual?

Yeah… I think I do eat faster. It’s not like when I’m sitting at the table with my family, where you talk a little, pass things around, actually taste what you’re eating.

At night it’s more like… I’m trying to get it done quick, before anyone wakes up or comes in and sees me. I’ll be standing there, just putting food in my mouth, barely tasting it. Like I’m rushing even though nobody’s chasing me, you know?
Do you feel upset, ashamed, or embarrassed about these nighttime eating episodes?

Yeah… embarrassed, for sure. I don’t like anyone seeing how much I can put away, so I kind of wait until my aunt and everybody in the house is asleep.

I’ll try to be quiet in the kitchen too, like closing cabinets slow, not making the microwave beep if I can help it. Which is stupid, I guess, because it’s my aunt’s house and she’s not mean about food or anything. She’s got this old clock in there that ticks really loud, and sometimes I’m more aware of that than anything else… but yeah, the main thing is I don’t want anybody walking in and seeing the amount.
